newsitem.title: USA: Lazard Freres, Wasserstein talked but no deal -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Lazard Freres, Wasserstein talked but no deal -WSJ.

text.p: Lazard Freres & Co recently held talks with investment boutique Wasserstein Perella & Co regarding Lazard buying or merging with Wasserstein but top Lazard partners rejected the idea, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition on Friday.

Lazard controlling shareholder Michel David-Weill was thought to have recently initiated talks with Bruce Wasserstein which centered on Wasserstein taking a senior role in the firm, the newspaper said.

But Lazard partners rejected the plan at a meeting in mid-April, according to people familiar with the meeting, the Journal reported. These people were quoted as saying many partners were against the prospect.
David-Weill and Wasserstein were quoted in the Journal as declining to comment.
Lazard Freres faces the planned departure of the investment bank's top dealmaker Felix Rohatyn, seen as being named U.S. Ambassador to France.

According to people on Wall Street, another name which came up in Lazard's discussions was Robert Greenhill, who was an investment banker at Morgan Stanley Group for a long time who also ran the Smith Barney securities arm of Travelers before leaving to start his own firm, the paper said.
Greenhill was also quoted as declining to comment.
